question: Tell me about a prompt change you made that caused a regression in production. How did you catch it, and how did you fix it?

question: If you multiply the loss for one class by a very large factor, which class will the model learn faster?
reference_points: Scaling a class's loss scales its gradient, so the optimizer prioritizes that class
It effectively raises the learning rate for that class's contribution
An extreme factor can destabilize training and hurt the other class
Use sensible class weights or focal loss tuned on validation data

question: When should you fine-tune a pretrained model versus use it as a frozen feature extractor, and what does freezing the head mean?
reference_points: Frozen extractor: cheap and safe for small data or a similar domain
Fine-tuning: better fit when the domain differs and enough data exists; costs more and can overfit
Freezing the head means its weights are not updated, while backbone layers may be trained
Usually train a new head first, then unfreeze gradually at a low learning rate

question: How would you implement a training loop for an object detection model?

Diagnose issues by visualizing predictions, checking label format and coordinates, and verifying the learning rate

question: At a high level, how do you build a large language model?

Decoder-only transformer pretrained on next-token prediction with distributed training
Alignment: supervised fine-tuning, then RLHF or preference optimization
Evaluate on benchmarks and safety tests; optimize and serve with quantization and batching

question: A system must search 12 million face embeddings for a new face quickly. How do you do it?
reference_points: Brute-force distance to all vectors is too slow
Use approximate nearest neighbor indexes: HNSW, IVF, Annoy, LSH, FAISS
Trade a small recall loss for large latency gains; shard and use GPUs if needed
Apply a distance threshold for match decisions and re-rank top candidates

question: How does a speech-to-text model like Whisper work, and how does it differ from text-to-speech?
reference_points: Audio is converted to log-Mel spectrograms and fed to a transformer encoder-decoder
The decoder generates text tokens autoregressively
Trained on large multilingual, weakly supervised audio-text data
TTS runs the opposite direction: text to acoustic features to waveform (vocoder)

question: How would you build a super-resolution pipeline to enhance image quality?
